goal: Stop a pull request from weakening the change record check that judges it (agent-kit H13, run 2026-11-22-protect-gates in lyddonb/quality). The check ran only from the pull request's own changes.yml, so the pull request could move the checker pin or change its flags.
changed: changes.yml also runs on pull_request_target. That run reads changes.yml and the checker pin from main, checks out the pull request's merge commit as data, and runs no code from it.
Both runs check that refs/pull/N/merge holds the pull request's current head, as ledger.yml in quality and finances does.
Step 1 of 2: a later pull request drops the pull_request trigger, once a real pull request has shown the base-branch run passing.

claims.claim: A later run with the same name doesn't override a failing run of a required check: both must pass.
claims.check: Scratch PR 36 here, on base 5d1a330: the base-branch ledger-verify failed, a same-name pull_request job passed three minutes later, GraphQL isRequired was true for both and mergeStateStatus stayed BLOCKED. Repeated under a ruleset on agent-kit PR 92.
claims.remaining: Measured in one order (failure first). A failure that finishes last is blocked by the same rule.

claims.claim: The pull_request_target run of change-record works on main.
claims.remaining: GitHub runs pull_request_target only from the default branch, so it can't run before this merges. The first pull request after the merge shows it; the step-2 PR cites that run.

next.item: Drop the pull_request trigger from changes.yml
next.why_now: Until then the pull request's own copy still runs beside the base copy, which costs a second job per PR
next.impact: One change-record run per PR, read only from main

release.none: CI only: what a contributor sees is a second change-record run on each pull request until step 2.
